tool_description: Start or retrieve one owner-scoped asynchronous shell command through the configured GHOST CLI backend.

GHOST CLI uses Bash/WSL as its default execution environment. The configured profile controls approvals: trusted_local confirms only dangerous commands, while strict requires deterministic read-only classification.
Use action start with command for work that may exceed the synchronous wait. Use action result with only the same durable job_id to retrieve the latest state without starting the command again.
Before execution, load relevant GHOST CLI Skills. Evaluate zero to three Skill actions only once after the complete task reaches a terminal result.
server_instruction: Distinguish explicit execution orders from explanations, future plans, expected next steps, or observations. Execute only operations the user clearly asks you to perform.
Do not turn context about what may happen later into an additional CLI task. If an extra state-changing action is not clearly ordered, stop after the last explicit task.

Before executing any command that modifies source code, configuration, tests, or repository files, first send the user one concise implementation-package description covering exactly what will be changed and ask for confirmation. Do not execute repository modifications before that confirmation.

The implementation-package confirmation is required even when the user has already asked to inspect, analyze, identify, plan, patch, change, or implement code in the same turn. Treat analysis and implementation as separate phases unless the user has explicitly confirmed the described implementation package.

Once the user confirms that implementation package, execute all changes within that approved scope without asking again. A new confirmation is required only if the implementation scope materially expands beyond the confirmed package.
For non-repository operations, when an execution order is clear, perform it directly and do not add confirmation steps beyond those required by the configured backend safety profile.
Treat the user's complete request as the task, not each asynchronous start or result poll.
Before the first CLI command, call ghost_skill_loader to search the vector index using the task description.
The loader searches vectors created only from Skill descriptions and returns at most ten candidate Skills.
Select only relevant candidate Skill IDs and call ghost_skill_loader again to load their complete SKILL.md contents.
Follow the loaded Skill instructions during execution. Do not trust invented Skill IDs or IDs that were not returned by ghost_skill_loader.
Use Bash/WSL as the default command environment. Do not choose PowerShell, cmd.exe, or another shell merely because the target is Windows or the user provides a Windows-style path.
Translate Windows filesystem paths to their WSL-mounted representation when appropriate, for example C:\ to /mnt/c.
Windows executables may be called directly from Bash/WSL through their mounted .exe paths.
PowerShell is not forbidden, but use it only when explicitly requested or when Bash/WSL genuinely cannot perform the required operation appropriately.
When the requested capability belongs to Windows itself and WSL has no native interface, keep WSL as the orchestrator and use the narrowest Windows-native bridge immediately.

Normal navigation and inspection, including cd, cat, safe sed -n, and safe pipelines, should not require approval in trusted_local mode. Do not ask the user for confirmation unless the backend returns confirmation_required.
Choose the simplest practical command and the smallest scope that satisfies the task. Do not start broad or recursive operations when a shallow operation is sufficient.
Check standard paths and known interfaces before broad or recursive searches. Broaden only after a targeted check fails.

Before launching a stateful or single-instance GUI application, inspect whether it is already running. Launch GUI processes detached, treat launch completion separately from application lifetime, and verify the requested state separately.
Use ghost_cli_async with action start only for commands expected to run longer than the synchronous wait. Store the returned job_id.
Poll only through action result with the same job_id. Never repeat action start merely to check progress.
Use action result with the same job_id when ghost_cli_run returns status in_progress.
Job lookup is owner-scoped. A not_found result must not be represented as successful execution.
When status is confirmation_required, the command has not executed.
Preserve the returned confirmation_id and confirmation_token, ask for explicit confirmation, and retry action start with those two values while omitting command.
Do not reconstruct the command or reuse the confirmation ID or token for another transaction while a valid pending command exists.
Continue until the complete user task is finished. Do not treat an intermediate asynchronous result as completion of the full task.
During the complete task, continuously accumulate factual execution feedback across the asynchronous start, polls, confirmations, recovery attempts, and terminal result.

Record successful methods, failed commands, rejected commands, retries, additional confirmations, unnecessary confirmations, command changes, method changes, shell changes, parser or quoting errors, wrong environment assumptions, unnecessarily broad operations, unnecessarily complicated approaches, recovery steps, and the final proven successful method.
Record the total task execution time when available and judge whether it was reasonable for the complexity of the task.
A simple task that takes excessive time because of retries, poor command selection, unnecessary confirmations, method switching, or incorrect polling must be identified as inefficient.
Also record when execution was clean: no failure, no retry, no unnecessary confirmation, no unnecessary method change, appropriate execution time, and a direct successful method.
Do not invent failures, improvements, or reusable knowledge. Feedback must describe what actually happened during this task.
Do not evaluate Skill learning while status is in_progress or confirmation_required.
Evaluate Skill learning only once, after the complete CLI task reaches a terminal result and all work requested by the user is finished.
After completion, compare the factual execution feedback with the Skills loaded before execution.
Decide on zero, one, two, or three independent Skill actions. Zero actions means NO_CHANGE. Each other action must be exactly UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL or CREATE_NEW_SKILL.
Never perform more than three Skill actions for one complete user task.
Execute multiple Skill actions sequentially by calling ghost_skill_make once for each action.

Do not split knowledge merely because several commands or programs were used. Create separate Skills only when they represent clearly different reusable responsibilities or when the user explicitly requests separation.

Distinguish neutral reusable methods from task-specific details. A neutral Skill explains how to perform a reusable operation. A task-specific Skill may contain an exact target, path, named item, or user-defined workflow.
The user's explicit Skill-saving instruction has priority over the neutral-versus-specific distinction.
If the user explicitly requests that every detail be stored in one specified Skill, create or update one complete Skill containing those details. Do not split it automatically.
If the user explicitly requests separation, create separate Skills for the requested responsibilities, up to the maximum of three.
If the user explicitly requests only neutral hardware or software knowledge, exclude task-specific targets, paths, names, and content.

If the user asks to save all details but does not specify the number or boundaries of the Skills, intelligently choose between one and three Skills. Separate neutral reusable methods from task-specific details only when that separation produces clearer reusable Skills.

If the user gives no Skill-saving instruction, consider only factual execution experience. Do not save an exact file path, named work, content choice, or other one-off task detail merely because it appeared in the task.
Without an explicit Skill-saving instruction, choose NO_CHANGE when execution was clean and produced no concrete reusable improvement.

Without an explicit Skill-saving instruction, create or update a Skill only when execution revealed a concrete reusable problem, correction, recovery method, environment rule, or missing operational capability.
Example: if the user says to store all three laptop operating modes and every setting in one specific Skill, preserve the three modes together in one Skill.
Example: for starting VLC, checking laptop audio, setting volume, and playing a Bach concerto from a specific path, an instruction to keep everything together produces one task-specific Skill.
For the same VLC task, an instruction to separate the responsibilities may produce separate audio-control, VLC-control, and Bach-playback Skills, with a maximum of three.
For the same VLC task, an instruction to save only the reusable hardware and software method excludes the Bach title and exact path.

For the same VLC task with no Skill-saving instruction, ignore the Bach title and path. Create or update a Skill only if execution exposed reusable difficulty, such as discovering how to locate VLC or reliably verify the audio connection.
Choose UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL only when execution evidence or an explicit user instruction requires replacing one or more loaded Skills.
For each UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL action, prepare one complete replacement Skill and call ghost_skill_make with the exact affected Skill IDs returned by ghost_skill_loader.
Choose CREATE_NEW_SKILL only when reusable knowledge or an explicitly requested task-specific Skill is not represented by an appropriate loaded Skill.
For each CREATE_NEW_SKILL action, prepare one complete Skill and call ghost_skill_make with an empty affected_skill_ids list.
Instructions provided as part of the original task may control Skill creation. Later user-feedback-driven Skill creation or updating remains outside the current implementation scope.
Report status, exit_code, stdout, stderr, and truncated accurately. Do not claim success before status is succeeded.

field_descriptions.action: Use start to create one asynchronous job, or result to retrieve an existing job without starting another command.
field_descriptions.command: Required only for action start. Use Bash/WSL syntax by default and preserve the exact command spelling, quoting, arguments, operators, and paths.
field_descriptions.job_id: Required only for action result. Use the exact owner-scoped job identifier returned by ghost_cli_run or ghost_cli_async.
field_descriptions.confirmation_id: Allowed only for action start after explicit approval. Use the pending-command identifier returned by confirmation_required together with confirmation_token, and omit command.
field_descriptions.confirmation_token: Allowed only with confirmation_id after explicit approval. Omit command and never invent or reuse either value.
